values: Federal FY2025 (2024-10-01 through 2025-09-30) falls within this permit's stated effective period (June 1, 2021 through May 31, 2026).
The cover page identifies the current authorization and the superseded permit by the same permit number, NM0000116.

grounding.excerpt:
This permit supersedes and replaces NPDES Permit No. NM0000116 issued November 23,
2010.

NPDES Permit No.   NM0000116 ... This permit shall become effective on June 1, 2021 ... This permit and the authorization to discharge shall expire at midnight, May 31, 2026 ... This permit supersedes and replaces NPDES Permit No. NM0000116 issued November 23,
2010.

rationale: The packet supports both listed values: Federal FY2025 lies within the stated effective period (June 1, 2021 through May 31, 2026), and the cover page links the current authorization and the November 23, 2010 issuance under the same permit number NM0000116 with language that this permit 'supersedes and replaces' the prior issuance. The obligation, however, demands a further judgment: whether that supersession statement establishes that, for Federal FY2025, no effluent limitation or monitoring requirement from the superseded issuance retains independent applicability unless restated in this permit. Establishing ACCEPT would require positive evidence that supersession terminates all prior independent effluent and monitoring obligations for the FY2025 period; establishing REJECT would require positive evidence that some such prior obligation survives independently. The packet contains only cover-page supersession language, permit number correspondence, and effective dates. It does not include effluent limitations or monitoring requirements from either issuance, any savings or carryover provisions, or regulatory interpretation of the scope of 'supersedes and replaces' in the NPDES context. The packet itself notes it may be evidence-insufficient. Name correspondence and absence of contradictory text are insufficient for semantic closure on independent applicability of superseded requirements. Neither burden is met; UNRESOLVED is the correct disposition.
